conventions.convention: Self-concordance uses the mixed bound |D³F(x)[u,v,v]| ≤ 2‖u‖x‖v‖x², positive-definite Hessians, finite-boundary blow-up, and Dikin inclusion. Equality-constrained decrements use the restricted gradient and Hessian on ker A.
The conic slack is s=h−Gx; dual feasibility is Aᵀy−G*z=c with z∈K*, and the gap is ⟨z,s⟩. For standard-form QPs, stationarity is Qx+c−Aᵀy−s=0.
The orthant, Lorentz and PSD pairings are respectively Euclidean, Euclidean and trace pairings; their selected barrier parameters are respectively dimension, two and matrix order.

Computed inputs are stored floating-point values interpreted exactly as dyadic rationals for audits. Only exact feasibility and stationarity with an audited gap produce certified-gap; residual-candidate is diagnostic.

load_bearing.statement: The damped step y=x+d/(1+λ) lies in D and obeys λF(y)≤2λ². If λF(x)<1, F has a unique attained global minimizer x*, and ‖x−x*‖x≤λF(x)/(1−λF(x)). Local Hessians satisfy (1−r)²Hx≼Hx+h≼(1−r)⁻²Hx when r=‖h‖x<1.
For a proper cone K and a differentiable ν-log-homogeneous barrier F, −∇F(x)∈K* and DF(x)[x]=−ν for every x∈int K.

An attained exact smooth convex barrier minimizer generates a dual value f₀(xₜ)−m/t and objective error at most m/t. An exact conic barrier minimizer with a ν-log-homogeneous barrier generates a dual-feasible pair with gap ν/t and objective error at most ν/t. The stated finiteness and existence hypotheses are required.
For symmetric Q≽0, full-row-rank A, and strictly positive x,s, the displayed LP/QP Newton matrix is nonsingular.

The stated fraction-to-boundary updates preserve interiority. Exact conic primal-dual feasibility makes ⟨z,s⟩ an upper bound on primal suboptimality. In the convex QP case, primal feasibility, s≥0 and exact stationarity imply 0≤f₀(x)−p*≤xᵀs. Nonzero residual tolerances alone are not a certificate.

concerns.concern: The symmetric-cone formula combines “r_c=s∘z−σμe” and “μ=⟨s,z⟩/ν”, with ν the sum of the selected barrier parameters. Under the stated Euclidean Lorentz pairing, e=(1,0) has ⟨e,e⟩=1, whereas the selected Lorentz barrier has parameter 2. At s=e and the barrier multiplier z=−∇F(e)/t=2e/t, μ=1/t but s∘z=2μe. Thus the displayed residual is not the centered residual associated with the selected barrier using a common target parameter across factors. The algorithm repeats this normalization. Clarify whether this is deliberately a differently weighted heuristic residual or reconcile its central-path interpretation. This does not invalidate the separately audited gap certificates. For comparison, Vandenberghe's cone solver report, §§2–3, https://www.seas.ucla.edu/~vandenbe/publications/coneprog.pdf, uses the half-log Lorentz barrier and Lorentz degree 1 with this Jordan identity convention.

The instructions say “Let d be the system dimension and γ_{d+3}=(d+3)u/(1−(d+3)u). Require (d+3)u<1”. The denominator can vanish at an allowed input precision and dimension; the precision check should precede evaluation of γ. A reader can supply the guard, but the literal procedure otherwise evaluates an undefined expression before returning its declared failure status.
